title: Chess understanding — Lucena seed ontology v1 (800–2000, skill-type modules)

modules.goal: See the board as it is: what is attacked, what is defended, what is free.
modules.label: Board Vision

modules.goal: Recognize and calculate the recurring forcing motifs.
modules.label: Tactical Patterns

modules.goal: Judge danger to both kings a move before it is real.
modules.label: King Safety & Attack

modules.goal: Choose moves by structure, activity and plans when nothing is forcing.
modules.label: Positional Judgment

modules.goal: Convert advantages and hold the fundamental endings.
modules.label: Technique & Endgames

modules.goal: The habits that decide games regardless of knowledge.
modules.label: Thinking Discipline

behaviors: before moving, names every undefended piece of both sides
spots when a move leaves a piece en prise, including their own
in own games, hanging-piece losses stop recurring

rubric.looks_like: finds a hanging piece only after the coach points at the square
finds hanging pieces when asked to scan, but misses them unprompted mid-line
flags loose pieces unprompted while discussing something else

concepts.label: Hanging pieces

behaviors: counts attackers and defenders on a contested square before capturing
notices when a 'defender' is overloaded, pinned, or of the wrong value
recognizes that trading a defender changes every count it was part of

rubric.looks_like: counts bodies only — misses value order and pinned defenders
counts correctly on the focus square but misses the second square the defender covered
narrates the full exchange sequence with values and spots the overloaded defender unprompted

concepts.label: Attackers vs defenders

behaviors: plays out a capture chain in order (cheapest first) before starting it
stops calculating a sequence when recapture order makes it clearly bad
judges 'is this pawn actually free?' correctly most of the time

rubric.looks_like: takes because a capture is available; surprised by the recapture
calculates two-piece exchanges reliably; loses the thread at three+
resolves multi-piece exchanges including zwischenzug possibilities

concepts.label: Capture sequences (SEE intuition)

behaviors: scans knight and pawn fork squares after every opponent piece move
creates double attacks deliberately, not just when they appear
sees queen dual-threat moves (mate + material) for both sides

rubric.looks_like: sees a fork when both targets are already attacked; walks into knight forks
spots fork opportunities in puzzles; misses the defensive scan in own games
prophylactically covers fork squares and engineers double attacks two moves ahead

concepts.label: Forks & double attack

behaviors: distinguishes absolute from relative pins and knows a relative pin can be broken
exploits pins by piling up rather than releasing the tension early
notices when their own 'defender' is pinned and doesn't actually defend

rubric.looks_like: sees the pin symbol on the board but still counts the pinned piece as a defender
exploits given pins; rarely sets up new ones deliberately
converts pins into wins methodically and breaks opponent pins at the right moment

concepts.label: Pins & skewers

behaviors: checks what opens when any piece moves off a line, for both sides
recognizes battery potential (piece in front of rook/bishop/queen) before it fires
calculates discovered checks to the end because 'the moving piece is free'

rubric.looks_like: hit by discoveries repeatedly; treats the front piece as safely placed
sees discoveries a move before they land; sets them up only from puzzles
builds batteries deliberately and prices the discovery into every exchange

concepts.label: Discovered attacks

behaviors: asks 'what is this piece doing?' before trading or driving it away
spots deflection and overload targets (a piece defending two things)
declines trades that would remove their own key defender

rubric.looks_like: trades whenever offered; the concept 'this knight had a job' is new information
identifies the defender's job when prompted with 'what was it guarding?'
hunts overloaded pieces unprompted and evaluates every trade by jobs, not values

concepts.label: Removing the defender

behaviors: tracks luft status for both kings as a standing condition, not a puzzle theme
spots when a defender of the back rank is deflectable
makes luft at the right moment — not too early (tempo) or too late (mate)

rubric.looks_like: knows the mate pattern in puzzles; loses games to it anyway
checks own back rank when queens and rooks come off their file
uses the opponent's back-rank weakness as a standing tactical resource in calculation

concepts.label: Back-rank weakness

behaviors: recognizes the preconditions of combinations: loose pieces, exposed king, aligned pieces
raises alertness when signals accumulate instead of playing by routine
knows when a position is quiet and calculation can relax

rubric.looks_like: calculates the same amount everywhere; tactics feel like lightning strikes
names signals in review ('two loose pieces — I should have looked')
visibly shifts gears in-game when the signal count rises

concepts.label: Reading tactical signals

behaviors: evaluates pawn-shield integrity before opening lines near their king
judges which pawn moves in front of the king are weakening vs necessary
counts attackers vs defenders in the king zone before grabbing material elsewhere

rubric.looks_like: pushes shield pawns for space without registering the king cost
keeps the shield intact but can't say when h3/h6 is actually fine
trades shield integrity for concrete gains only with a counted attack/defense balance

concepts.label: King shelter & luft

behaviors: counts pieces that can join the attack vs pieces that can defend before committing
opens lines toward the enemy king only when the count favors the attack
defends by trading attackers and keeping the shield, not by grabbing pawns

rubric.looks_like: attacks because it feels right; sacrifices on vibes
counts correctly when asked; overestimates own attack in-game
declines unsound attacks and explains the missing attacker; defends without panic

concepts.label: Attacking the king soundly

behaviors: names the available pawn breaks for both sides in any structure
prepares a break (pieces behind it) instead of playing it bare
recognizes when no break exists and piece play must change the structure first

rubric.looks_like: shuffles pieces in closed positions; 'break' is vocabulary, not a plan
identifies the thematic break when asked; timing is guesswork
builds the game around preparing the right break and preventing the opponent's

concepts.label: Pawn breaks

behaviors: spots holes (squares no pawn can ever defend) as they are created
maneuvers a knight toward an outpost across several moves
avoids creating holes in their own camp for a one-move convenience

rubric.looks_like: sees the strong knight only after it arrives
identifies holes in review; in-game the maneuver loses to impatience
trades and pushes pawns with the square map in mind, both colors

concepts.label: Weak squares & outposts

behaviors: identifies their worst-placed piece when there is no forcing move
judges trades by activity delta, not just material equality
notices when a 'developed' piece is doing nothing and re-routes it

rubric.looks_like: moves whichever piece has an obvious move; activity is invisible
names the worst piece when asked; the improving plan needs prompting
quiet moves are activity investments and they can say the payoff aloud

concepts.label: Piece activity — improve the worst piece

behaviors: contests a file before the opponent doubles on it, not after
knows a file matters only if it has entry squares
places bishops on diagonals that point at something that matters

rubric.looks_like: rooks stay on starting squares until move 30
takes the open file when free; concedes it without a fight when contested
fights for files with entry squares and ignores decorative ones

concepts.label: Open files & diagonals

behaviors: asks 'what does my opponent want?' before choosing their own move
spends a tempo to stop the opponent's best plan when it outweighs their own
distinguishes prophylaxis from passivity — prevention with purpose

rubric.looks_like: opponent's last move is read as an event, not an intention
states the opponent's idea when asked, then plays their own plan anyway
unprompted: 'first I stop …, then my plan is unstoppable'

concepts.label: Prophylaxis

behaviors: evaluates a trade by what remains on the board, not what leaves it
keeps attackers when attacking, trades when defending or ahead
checks the resulting endgame before entering a forced simplification

rubric.looks_like: accepts every equal-value trade reflexively
applies 'trade when ahead' but simplifies into losing pawn endings
names the piece that must stay and the ending they're steering toward

concepts.label: What to trade and why

behaviors: shuts down counterplay before grabbing more material
trades pieces, not pawns, when ahead — and can say why
keeps calculating checks and threats when winning instead of relaxing

rubric.looks_like: eval graph: +4 then the swindle; grabs pawns while the opponent's rook activates
converts clean +5 endings; +2 middlegames still drift
wins won games with the boring move; counterplay dies first, always

concepts.label: Converting winning positions

behaviors: executes the Lucena bridge and states why each move exists
holds Philidor's third-rank defense without move-order help
knows which side of the draw/win line a simplified rook ending falls on before entering it

rubric.looks_like: shuffles checks in a won rook ending until the 50-move counter looms
wins Lucena with hints; Philidor collapses under an unexpected try
plays both flawlessly and uses the knowledge as an in-game simplification target

concepts.label: Rook endings — Lucena & Philidor

behaviors: calculates opposition and key squares in K+P vs K without guessing
counts races (pawn vs pawn) by squares, not intuition
treats every simplification into a pawn ending as a forced-result decision

rubric.looks_like: K+P vs K result is a coin flip
knows the opposition rule; miscounts races under pressure
converts and holds textbook endings on autopilot; enters them only on purpose

concepts.label: Pawn endings — opposition & counting

behaviors: runs checks-captures-threats for the opponent before releasing every committal move
asks 'what did that move change?' after every opponent move
blunder rate in own games trends down over the training period

rubric.looks_like: moves on first idea; the scan happens only in puzzles
scans in slow games; skips it in rapid or when 'obviously' winning
the scan is invisible and constant; one-move blunders are rare events

concepts.label: The blunder check

behaviors: derives a plan from structure (breaks, weak squares, worst piece) rather than move-to-move impulse
states the position's demands in one sentence before choosing a candidate
abandons a plan when the structure changes, not when it gets boring

rubric.looks_like: 'I develop and see what happens' persists to move 25
produces a plan when the coach asks; own games show plan fragments
every quiet position gets a stated plan traceable to a structural fact

concepts.label: Forming a plan in quiet positions

exit_test.desc: Given a fresh own loss (unseen by the coach), independently identify the decisive mistake, name the concept behind it, and show the refutation line — then verify against the engine pass.
exit_test.label: Decisive-moment audit of an own loss

exit_test.desc: Solve a 20-position mixed set (forks, pins, discoveries, deflection, back-rank) at rating-appropriate difficulty, ≥80%, naming the motif before the move.
exit_test.label: Mixed tactical recognition under mild clock

exit_test.desc: In three positions from own games, enumerate every job of the piece about to be traded and judge the trade; engine-verified.
exit_test.label: Trade audit

exit_test.desc: From a +3 middlegame position, beat maximum engine resistance at reduced strength appropriate to rating, prioritizing counterplay suppression; no swindle allowed.
exit_test.label: Convert a won position against resistance

exit_test.desc: Win the Lucena position and hold the Philidor defense against the engine, explaining the purpose of each key move.
exit_test.label: Lucena & Philidor on demand

exit_test.desc: In two quiet positions, state the correct plan (break / worst piece / file) and defend it Socratically; consistent with engine top lines over a 5-move horizon.
exit_test.label: Plan from structure
